question: Does net.fetch / session.fetch crash or misbehave while an extension declaring webRequest and/or declarativeNetRequest is loaded in that session, on plain Electron 44.0.0 (no product code)?
reference: electron/electron PR #45050, 'fix: checks in extensions webRequest when using net.fetch'
method: Each matrix cell is a separate headless Electron process (a crash ends the process). Probe writes its results file after every step, so a segfault still shows exactly which call was in flight. A local http server on 127.0.0.1 served every request; server-side request logs corroborate whether traffic ever left the process. Crashes were independently confirmed via coredumpctl (all SIGSEGV in the electron binary, timed to the run window).

summary.conclusion: UNSAFE as originally planned: with no embedder webRequest listener on the target session, net.fetch/session.fetch/net.request all reliably SIGSEGV the whole Electron process the instant the extension's proxied loader factory is hit -- for every extension shape tested (declarativeNetRequest alone, declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess, MV3 webRequest, MV2 webRequest+webRequestBlocking) and on both session.defaultSession and a session.fromPartition() session.
summary.workaround_found: Installing an embedder-side session.webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders listener on the SAME session BEFORE loading the extension prevents the crash entirely (reproduced twice on the MV3 webRequest case, and once on the worst-case MV2 blocking case). Orivon already installs such a listener on the default session, so Orivon's own current setup is not exposed to this crash as long as that listener is installed before any extension with webRequest/declarativeNetRequest permissions is loaded into that session, and before any net.fetch call. This is an empirical workaround from a plain-Electron probe, not a confirmed root-cause fix -- treat as provisional until read against the actual PR #45050 patch.

R2-dnr-default.lastStep: waitedForServiceWorker (crashed on the following net.fetch call)

R2b-dnr-default-retry.note: repeat run with per-call start markers: crash pinpointed to inside net.fetch() itself

R7-dnr-partition.note: confirms it's the SESSION holding the extension that crashes, not net.fetch globally

R3-webrequest-mv3-default.extension: c: MV3 webRequest, non-blocking onBeforeRequest listener <all_urls>
R3-webrequest-mv3-default.lastStep: waitedForServiceWorker (crashed on the following net.fetch call)

R4-dnr-hostaccess-default.lastStep: waitedForServiceWorker (crashed on the following net.fetch call)

R5-mv2-webrequest-default.lastStep: waitedForServiceWorker (crashed on the following net.fetch call)

R11-webrequest-mv3-default-extralistener.note: embedder's own ses.webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders installed BEFORE loadExtension -- crash disappears

R11b-webrequest-mv3-default-extralistene.note: repeat of R11, same result -- reproducible

R12-mv2-webrequest-default-extralistener.note: workaround holds even for the most aggressive extension type tested

notes: The crash is not specific to extensions declaring the 'webRequest' permission: declarativeNetRequest-only (case b) and declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess (case d) crash identically, even though neither uses the webRequest API. Any of the four extension shapes tested is sufficient.
The crash site is precisely inside the net.fetch()/ses.fetch() call: per-call 'starting' markers (flushed to disk before the call) show the process died mid-call, not before or after.

For the partition-session runs, a plain net.fetch() on session.defaultSession (which has no extension loaded) never crashed -- the crash is scoped to the session the extension is loaded into, consistent with the PR's description of a per-session/per-extension proxied URLLoaderFactory.

net.request and BrowserWindow page loads were never reached in any crashing run (the very first net.fetch/ses.fetch call always crashed first), so this probe cannot separately confirm whether net.request alone (independent of net.fetch/ses.fetch) would also crash; by symmetry with the underlying mechanism (same proxied loader factory) it is reasonable to expect the same failure, but that was not directly observed.
MV2 extension with webRequestBlocking loaded via session.loadExtension without complaint on Electron 44.0.0 (no rejection recorded).

All crashes are SIGSEGV in the electron binary itself (confirmed via coredumpctl, not just the shell's 'Segmentation fault' message), i.e. the whole browser process, not an isolated renderer/utility crash.
